questions.work:

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, match or one word).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) In a purely capacitive circuit the current leads the voltage by ______. (b) In a purely inductive circuit the average power dissipated is ______.
Fill in the blanks: (a) The induced current opposes the cause producing it — this is ______'s law. (b) Transformer cores are laminated to reduce ______ currents.
Complete: (a) Inductive reactance X_L = ______. (b) Capacitive reactance X_C = ______.
State True or False: (a) A transformer works on dc. (b) A step-up transformer has more turns in the secondary.
questions.answer:
(a) False — it needs a changing flux (ac).
(b) True.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: A bar falling through the hollow region of a thick copper cylinder experiences a retarding force. What can you conclude about the bar? Explain.
questions.answer: The bar is a magnet. As it falls, the changing flux induces eddy currents in the copper which, by Lenz's law, oppose its motion — hence the retarding force. An unmagnetised bar would fall freely.

questions.q: State Lenz's law. Show that it follows from conservation of energy.
questions.answer: The induced current flows in a direction that opposes the change producing it. If it aided the change, a small motion would produce ever-growing current and energy from nothing; opposing it means work must be done, which becomes electrical energy.

questions.q: A coil carries 1 A on 100 V dc and 0.6 A on 100 V ac. Explain, and find its reactance.
questions.answer:
On dc only resistance acts: R = 100/1 = 100 Ω. On ac the inductive reactance also acts: Z = 100/0.6 ≈ 167 Ω.
X_L = √(Z² − R²) = √(167² − 100²) ≈ 133 Ω.

questions.q: State Faraday's laws of electromagnetic induction.
questions.answer:
First law: whenever the magnetic flux linked with a circuit changes, an emf is induced in it.
Second law: the induced emf equals the rate of change of flux linkage: e = −N dφ/dt.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: State Faraday's laws of electromagnetic induction and explain them with an example.
questions.answer:
First law: an emf is induced whenever the flux linked with a coil changes. Second law: e = −N dφ/dt.
Example: pushing a bar magnet into a coil connected to a galvanometer gives a deflection. Pulling it out deflects the other way, and moving it faster gives a bigger deflection. When the magnet is still there is no deflection, because the flux is not changing.

questions.q: A transformer is to run machines needing (i) 25000 V and (ii) 25 V from a 250 V, 50 Hz supply. Name the transformers and give their turns ratios.
questions.answer:
(i) Step-up transformer, Nₚ : Nₛ = 250 : 25000 = 1 : 100.
(ii) Step-down transformer, Nₚ : Nₛ = 250 : 25 = 10 : 1.
The primary is connected to the supply and the secondary to the machine.

questions.q: What is a transformer? How does it work? Give three causes of energy loss in it.
questions.answer:
A device that changes ac voltage (step up or step down) using mutual induction.
Working: ac in the primary makes a changing flux in the laminated soft-iron core, which induces an emf in the secondary: Vₛ/Vₚ = Nₛ/Nₚ.
Losses: (1) copper loss I²R in the windings; (2) eddy-current loss in the core; (3) hysteresis loss; also flux leakage.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: A transformer has 200 turns in its primary and 1000 in its secondary, with resistances 0.4 Ω and 2 Ω. The secondary output is 13.5 kW at 1200 V and the efficiency is 90%. Find (i) the input voltage, (ii) the input power, (iii) the primary and secondary currents and (iv) the power lost in the primary.
questions.answer:
(i) Vₚ = Vₛ × Nₚ/Nₛ = 1200 × 200/1000 = 240 V.
(ii) P_in = P_out/η = 13500/0.9 = 15000 W = 15 kW.
(iii) Iₚ = P_in/Vₚ = 15000/240 = 62.5 A; Iₛ = P_out/Vₛ = 13500/1200 = 11.25 A.
(iv) Primary copper loss = Iₚ²Rₚ = 62.5² × 0.4 ≈ 1562.5 W.
Total loss = 1500 W = 10% of the input.

or.q: A 60 mH inductor, 50 µF capacitor and 20 Ω resistor are in series across an ac source of peak 210 V and ω = 400 rad/s. Find the impedance, the rms current and the rms voltages across L, C and R. Does the current lead or lag?

questions.q: A metal rod of length l rotates with frequency ν about one end, which is at the centre of a circular metal ring, the other end touching the ring. A uniform field B is parallel to the axis. Obtain the emf between the centre and the ring.
questions.answer:
Take an element dr at distance r; its speed is v = ωr. The emf across it is de = Bv dr = Bωr dr.
e = ∫₀ˡ Bωr dr = ½Bωl².
With ω = 2πν: e = πνBl².

questions.q: An ac voltage e = e₀ sin ωt is applied to a series LCR circuit. Draw the phasor diagram and obtain the impedance and the phase angle. When is the current maximum?
questions.answer:
The same current I flows through all three. V_R is in phase with I, V_L leads I by 90° and V_C lags I by 90°.
From the phasor diagram: V² = V_R² + (V_L − V_C)² ⇒ Z = √[R² + (X_L − X_C)²], with X_L = ωL and X_C = 1/ωC.
Phase angle: tan φ = (X_L − X_C)/R.
The current is maximum at resonance, X_L = X_C, i.e. ω₀ = 1/√(LC), when Z = R.
